title: A ring with finitely many maximal ideals and nil Jacobson radical is the product of its localizations
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring with finitely many maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_1,\dots,\mathfrak n_r$ such that every element of the Jacobson radical $\mathfrak n_1\cap\dots\cap\mathfrak n_r$ is nilpotent. Then every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal, and the canonical ring map $B\to\prod_{i=1}^rB_{\mathfrak n_i}$, $b\mapsto(b/1)_i$, into the product of the localizations at the maximal ideals is an isomorphism (of $B$-algebras, hence of $A$-algebras for every ring map $A\to B$); each $B_{\mathfrak n_i}$ is a local ring.
